blocks.text: The leading newly prioritized issue is **CVE-2026-123903 (VMware vSphere Foundation)**, a critical authentication bypass flaw. Malicious exploitation was not confirmed by tracked sources. blocks.text: **Top five actions:** (1) Apply the vendor fix for VMware vSphere Foundation (CVE-2026-123903); (2) apply the vendor fix for WP Media WP Rocket (CVE-2026-125812); (3) apply the vendor fix for Camunda (CVE-2026-77230); (4) close previously reported Project MONAI MONAI Label, Vates Xen Orchestra, N-able MailAssure and Idunno AntiCsrf KEV exposure; (5) examine VMware vSphere Foundation hosts for unauthorized administrative access and configuration changes.

**CVE-2026-123903 - VMware vSphere Foundation authentication bypass (CVSS 9.8).** VMware vCenter contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in the VMware Directory Service. Broadcom has evaluated the severity of this issue to be in the Critical severity range with a maximum CVSSv3 base score of 9.8. Affected releases: not yet published in NVD configuration data. Fixed package release: none identified in tracked sources. Attack path: network-accessible; no authentication required; no user interaction required.

**CVE-2026-77230 - Camunda unsafe deserialization (CVSS 9.2).** Camunda 8.8.0 before 8.8.47, 8.9.0 before 8.9.29, 8.10.0 before 8.10.10, and 8.11.0-alpha1 contain an insecure deserialization vulnerability in the persistent web session feature, which stores session attributes as Java-serialized data in secondary storage and deserializes them via an ObjectInputStream without an ObjectInputFilter. Affected releases: not yet published in NVD configuration data. Fixed package release: none identified in tracked sources. Attack path: network-accessible; no authentication required; no user interaction required.

No new zero-day or in-the-wild exploitation reports beyond CISA KEV were identified for newly prioritized CVEs in tracked sources (Google Project Zero, ENISA EUVD, VulnCheck KEV). No reliable campaign-specific IP addresses, hashes or domains were identified.

No new CISA KEV additions were verified in the reporting window. The latest additions remain the 10 entries added November 25, 2026: Danfoss AK-SM 800A Series, Danfoss AK-SM 800A Series, Danfoss AK-SM 800A Series, Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) Juniper Session Smart Conductor and Session Smart Router, Mitel MiCollab and Mitel MiCollab. The federal remediation deadline for those entries is **November 28, 2026**. This deadline applies to covered federal agencies under applicable requirements; it is not a universal private-sector mandate.

**Defensive hunting:** for VMware vSphere Foundation (CVE-2026-123903), review administrative logins, newly created accounts or API tokens, and configuration changes made without a matching change record; for WP Media WP Rocket (CVE-2026-125812), inspect unexpected file writes outside the application's data directories, new web-accessible files, modified application code, altered SSH authorized_keys files and suspicious scheduled jobs; for Camunda (CVE-2026-77230), inspect unexpected child processes of the service, new scheduled jobs or services, and unusual outbound connections from the host.
